definitions.explanation: Having a large diameter or girth.

examples.japanese: {太|ふと}いペンで{書|か}いてください。
examples.english: Please write with a thick pen.

examples.japanese: {太|ふと}い{枝|えだ}が{道|みち}をふさいでいた。
examples.english: A thick branch was blocking the road.

examples.japanese: {太|ふと}い{字|じ}で{名前|なまえ}を{書|か}いてください。
examples.english: Please write your name in bold letters.

examples.japanese: レポートの{題名|だいめい}は{太|ふと}い{文字|もじ}にしてください。
examples.english: Please make the report title bold.

notes:
{太|ふと}い is an i-adjective describing thickness or large diameter.

FORMS:
- Adverbial: {太|ふと}く
- Noun form: {太|ふと}さ (thickness)
- Verb: {太|ふと}る (to get fat)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {太|ふと}い{木|き}: thick tree
- {太|ふと}い{線|せん}: thick/bold line
- {足|あし}が{太|ふと}い: to have thick legs
- {太|ふと}い{声|こえ}: deep/booming voice
- {太|ふと}{字|じ}: bold text

CONTRAST:
- {太|ふと}い ↔ {細|ほそ}い (thin, slender)

FOR PEOPLE:
Use {太|ふと}っている (to be fat) rather than {太|ふと}い when describing overweight people. {太|ふと}い{人|ひと} can sound blunt or rude.
